units: <cite ref="Arakhin 18a:39">Arakh. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>ולידון בכְבוֹדוֹ</he> (Ar. <he>בכבידו</he>) and that the value of a limb be judged according to its importance (vitality); ib. 4ᵇ; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 114a">B. Mets. 114ᵃ</cite>
<cite ref="Berakhot 19b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>משום כְּבוֹד מלכים</he> on account of the respect due to royalty.

<cite ref="Berakhot 19b:9">Ib.</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 37b:16">Men. 37ᵇ</cite> <he>גדול כְּ׳ הבריות וכ׳</he> human dignity (in proper appearance) is very important, for it may even suspend a Biblical law. Ber. l. c. <he>ואינו לפי כְבוֹרוֹ</he> and it is not becoming his dignity (to drive an ass).
<cite ref="Sotah 13a:12">Sot. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>הניחו לו כְּבוֹדוֹ במלכים יותר וכ׳</he> let him alone, the honor shown to him (Jacob) by princes is higher than that by private men.
<cite ref="Sotah 13a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>נהגו בהן כ׳</he> they treated them with respect.
<cite ref="Nedarim 39b:14">Ned. 39ᵇ</cite> <he>בכְבוֹדִי לא מחיתם בכְ׳ וכ׳</he> as long as My honor was concerned, you did not interfere, and when the honor of a human being is at stake &c.

Ab. IV, 12 יהי כְ׳ תלמידך וכ׳ let the honor of thy pupil be as dear to thee as thine own, and thy fellow student’s honor as that of thy teacher; a. v. fr.—כסא הכ׳, v. כִּסֵּא. מחל על כבודו to forego due honors, v. מָחַל.
